name: taro leaves
swap_tip: Can't find taro leaves? English spinach works, though it's milder and cooks faster – reduce cooking time to 30 minutes.

name: duruka
swap_tip: Can't find duruka? Use asparagus; it's milder but cooks in the same time.

name: banana leaves
swap_tip: Can't find banana leaves? Wrap in foil instead, though you'll lose the traditional flavour.

name: cassava
swap_tip: Can't find cassava? Use potato, though the texture will be a bit softer.

name: dalo
swap_tip: Can't find dalo? Use potato; it cooks in about the same time and has a similar texture when soft.

name: kousa
review_note: kousa is Arabic for zucchini (pilot review)

name: lolo
review_note: lolo is Fijian for coconut milk/cream (pilot review)

name: lamb shanks
swap_tip: Can't find lamb shanks? Use 800 g diced lamb shoulder; it'll cook in about 2 hours on high instead.

name: dried dates
swap_tip: Can't find dried jujubes? Use 1 extra tbsp honey instead for sweetness.

name: sashimi-grade fish
swap_tip: Can't find sashimi-grade fish? Ask your fishmonger for the freshest white fish available, or use very fresh salmon.

name: parsnips
swap_tip: Can't find parsnips? Use extra carrot or swap for potato—they'll all soften beautifully.

name: ackee
swap_tip: Most Caribbean shops stock tinned ackee. If you can't find it, this dish won't be the same, but a scrambled egg with the same vegetables will give you a similar breakfast.

name: miyeok
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: alias kept (same thing for diets and shopping)

name: smoked haddock fillet
swap_tip: Can't find smoked haddock? Use any smoked white fish, or even fresh haddock, though it won't have the same depth.

name: ikan bilis
swap_tip: Dried ikan bilis are smaller and more delicate than canned anchovies; if you can only find canned anchovies, use fewer and rinse them first.

name: jarred grape leaves
swap_tip: Can't find jarred grape leaves? Some delis stock fresh ones, or use dolmades (pre-made) if you need a shortcut.

name: candlenuts
swap_tip: Can't find candlenuts? Use macadamias or raw peanuts—they help thicken the sauce.

name: perch
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: alias kept (same thing for diets and shopping)

name: egusi
swap_tip: Can't find egusi? Crushed roasted peanuts work in a pinch, but egusi gives the authentic silky texture.

name: quesillo
swap_tip: Quesillo is Oaxaca's stretchy melting cheese. Use fresh mozzarella or halloumi if you can't find it.

name: chapulines
swap_tip: Can't find chapulines (dried grasshoppers)? Use roasted peanuts, though you'll lose the traditional Oaxacan taste.

name: urad dal
swap_tip: Can't find urad dal? Just skip it—the dosa will still taste good. The dal adds a slight crackle to the tempering, but it's optional.
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: black gram lentils; no gluten

name: berbere
swap_tip: Can't find berbere? Mix 2 tbsp paprika with 1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp ground cumin, and 1 tsp ground coriander.

name: hilsa fillets
swap_tip: Hilsa has a distinctive oily flesh and soft bones. Use sashimi-grade salmon or fresh mackerel for a similar richness; the cooking time remains the same.

name: nozawana
swap_tip: Can't find nozawana? Use young mustard greens or turnip greens; the flavour is peppery but similar.

name: snoek
swap_tip: Can't find snoek? Use whole kingfish, mackerel or snapper—anything firm and oily that holds up on the coals.

name: perilla leaves
swap_tip: Can't find perilla leaves? Thai basil has a similar fresh, peppery quality.

name: tempeh
swap_tip: Can't find tempeh? Firm tofu works, but tempeh's nutty flavour is worth seeking out at Asian grocers.

name: żur
swap_tip: Can't find żur? Mix 2 tbsp plain flour with 150 ml warm water and let it sit for 24 hours before using, though it won't be as sour. Or use 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar mixed with water instead.

name: wattleseed
swap_tip: Can't find wattleseed? Use a mixture of ground cumin and finely ground dark roasted coffee or cocoa for an earthy, nutty flavour.

name: milkfish
swap_tip: Can't find milkfish? Use barramundi or any firm white fish fillet of similar size, though the flavour won't be quite the same.

name: molokhia leaves
swap_tip: Can't find molokhia? Use frozen spinach (200 g) or fresh spinach (300 g), though the flavour won't be quite the same.

name: cockles
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: alias kept (same thing for diets and shopping)

name: arepas
swap_tip: Can't find arepas? Cornbread or polenta-based flatbread works in a pinch, though arepas are worth seeking out in the freezer aisle or bakery.

name: young green jackfruit
swap_tip: Can't find young jackfruit? Young papaya will cook faster (30–40 minutes instead of 90) but gives a similar texture and mild flavour.

name: tarhana paste
swap_tip: No tarhana? Use 1 tbsp tomato paste mixed with 1 tbsp red lentils, but the flavour will be different—tarhana's the real thing.

name: burdock
swap_tip: Can't find burdock? Use parsnip cut into matchsticks; it cooks a little faster.

name: poppy seed paste
swap_tip: Can't find poppy seed paste? Grind 3 tbsp raw poppy seeds with 1 tbsp water to a paste, or use tahini for a different but pleasant result.

name: agave leaves
swap_tip: Can't find agave leaves? Banana leaves work just as well and keep the meat moist while it braises.

name: sorrel
swap_tip: Fresh sorrel is tart and lemony. You can use baby spinach instead, but add the juice of half a lemon to the pot when you add the greens to get a similar brightness.

name: popiah skin
swap_tip: Can't find popiah skin? Use rice paper, but soak each sheet briefly in warm water first to soften it.

name: trout
swap_tip: Use any firm white fish fillet, though whole fish makes the dish more special.

name: besan
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: chickpea flour; no gluten

name: fresh ginseng
swap_tip: Can't find fresh ginseng? A piece of ginger won't taste the same, but it will still make a warming broth.

name: quandong
swap_tip: Can't find quandong? Use fresh or stewed stone fruit like peaches or apricots for sweetness, though you'll lose the tart native flavour.

name: nopales
swap_tip: Can't find nopales? Use 600 g zucchini, diced; it won't have quite the same flavour, but the texture and cooking time are similar.

name: grouper
swap_tip: Can't find fresh grouper? Barramundi or snapper works beautifully – adjust cooking time by a minute or two depending on size.

name: gat
swap_tip: Can't find gat? Use mustard greens or other Asian mustard leaf varieties; the taste will be slightly less peppery.

name: dasheen
swap_tip: Can't find dasheen (taro)? Use sweet potato or regular potato instead.

name: green banana
swap_tip: Can't find green bananas? Use regular bananas, though the texture won't be quite as firm.

name: pandan leaves
swap_tip: Can't find pandan leaves? Use a few mint leaves or a tiny drop of pandan extract (but pandan is worth seeking out—it's what makes cendol properly green and fragrant).

name: tripe
swap_tip: Can't find tripe? Use diced pork shoulder; increase cooking time to 1 hour 15 minutes until tender.

name: olluco
swap_tip: Can't find olluco? Use waxy potatoes or oca; they're starchy and hold their shape like olluco does.

name: wambatu
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: alias kept (same thing for diets and shopping)

name: epazote
swap_tip: Can't find epazote? Use fresh coriander for a different but fresh flavour, or simply leave it out.

name: catfish
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: alias kept (same thing for diets and shopping)

name: kerisik
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: alias kept (same thing for diets and shopping)

name: pierogi
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: dumplings; fillings vary, so tagged strictly

name: broad beans
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: fava beans, not cannellini

name: freekeh
swap_tip: Can't find freekeh? Use brown rice instead, though you'll lose the smoky, nutty flavour.

name: saltfish
swap_tip: Can't find saltfish? Use thick white fish fillet (cod or barramundi) and skip the soaking and boiling step—just flake and fold in gently at the end.

name: nduja
swap_tip: No nduja? Use 150 g pancetta, finely chopped, plus 1 tsp chilli flakes stirred in with the garlic—it won't be quite the same but it's close.

name: niter kibbeh
swap_tip: Can't find niter kibbeh? Use butter, though you'll miss the warm spice notes.

name: kina
swap_tip: Can't find kina? Scallops work, though they're richer—serve them raw and thinly sliced, or lightly seared.
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: sea urchin roe; not vegetarian

name: pāua
swap_tip: Can't find fresh pāua? Scallops work in a pinch, though they won't have the same kaupapa (story). Check your local kai moana supplier first.

name: ndolé
swap_tip: Can't find ndolé? Use spinach or other leafy greens, though the flavour will be milder and less bitter.
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: bitterleaf greens (the leaf itself)

name: pink pralines
swap_tip: Can't find pink pralines? Use blanched almonds folded through praline or nougat paste for a similar texture.

name: buah keluak
swap_tip: Can't find buah keluak? Use candlenuts or macadamia nuts, though the flavor won't be quite as dark and earthy.
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: seed of the kepayang tree; kept as tree nut to be safe

name: oyster omelette sauce
swap_tip: Can't find oyster omelette sauce? Mix 1 tbsp tapioca starch or cornflour with 150 ml water, then season with salt and white pepper.
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: sweet starch-thickened sauce; tagged strictly

name: pig's blood cake
swap_tip: Can't find pig's blood cake? Use firm tofu; it won't be quite the same but the QQ texture works too.
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: pork blood with rice

name: khoya
swap_tip: Can't find khoya? Use 50 g softened butter mixed with 50 g powdered milk, though the texture won't be quite as authentic.

name: mentaiko
swap_tip: Can't find mentaiko? Use smoked salmon or tinned tuna mixed with a squeeze of sriracha.

name: vine leaves
swap_tip: Can't find vine leaves? Use large basil leaves, but the flavour won't be quite the same.

name: palm nuts
review_note: Claude, 8 Oct: oil palm fruit, not a tree nut

name: pork liver
swap_tip: Can't find pork liver? Chicken liver works, but use only 300 g and reduce cooking time to 20 minutes.

name: pork heart
swap_tip: Pork heart can be hard to find. Ask your butcher, or substitute with extra pork liver or beef heart.

name: panela
swap_tip: Can't find panela? Use brown sugar or regular sugar, though it won't have quite the same molasses depth.
